title: Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act

claims.claim: Lets federal agencies pause payments that show signs of fraud.
claims.sourceSpan: The head of an agency shall take a corrective action to temporarily delay, condition, or segment a disbursement request before the certification of a payment voucher under section 3325

claims.claim: Lets the Treasury pause or split up payments that show signs of fraud.
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary shall promptly notify the relevant certifying official of an order to return a certified payment voucher submitted to a disbursing official under section 3325 and issue a corrective action order to the head of an agency
claims.note: Treasury = Secretary of the Treasury (def. 3337(j)(4)).

claims.claim: "split up payments" (i.e. segment).
claims.sourceSpan: temporarily delay, condition, or segment a disbursement request

claims.claim: The payments at issue "show signs of fraud" (elevated fraud risk).
claims.sourceSpan: has sufficient reason to determine that the payment presents an elevated risk of fraud based on a fraud-risk indicator

claims.claim: Requires payees to be notified.
claims.sourceSpan: Promptly provide to the payee

claims.claim: Payees given a chance to contest.
claims.sourceSpan: to contest any factual inaccuracy or provide clarifying information during the corrective action review period

claims.claim: The payment is due within 30 days.
claims.sourceSpan: Issue such payment not later than 30 days after a determination to take a corrective action is made by the head of the agency
claims.note: Figure (30 days) verbatim. Soft gloss: 3337(d)(3) makes the 30-day issuance conditional on the agency determining the payment does NOT present an elevated fraud/improper-payment risk; a payment still deemed fraudulent is not released. Plain-English "due within 30 days" slightly overstates for non-cleared payments. Not material; the sections[] detail carries the nuance.

claims.claim: Authorizes agencies and the Treasury to pause or segment federal payments flagged for fraud risk.
claims.sourceSpan: The head of an agency shall take a corrective action to temporarily delay, condition, or segment a disbursement request

claims.claim: with payee notice
claims.sourceSpan: Promptly provide to the payee

claims.claim: and time limits
claims.sourceSpan: Issue such payment not later than 30 days after a determination to take a corrective action is made by the head of the agency
claims.note: Time limits present: 2 days, 30 days, 7 days.

claims.claim: Pausing Risky Payments
claims.sourceSpan: Authority to pause payments for further review and corrective action

claims.claim: Agencies must pause or segment payments flagged for fraud risk.
claims.sourceSpan: The head of an agency shall take a corrective action to temporarily delay, condition, or segment a disbursement request
claims.note: Mandatory: "shall" = "must".

claims.claim: Treasury can return a payment voucher and order corrective action.
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary shall promptly notify the relevant certifying official of an order to return a certified payment voucher submitted to a disbursing official under section 3325 and issue a corrective action order to the head of an agency
claims.note: Describes granted authority; source uses "shall" once the Secretary makes a determination. "can" acceptable authority framing.

claims.claim: Triggered by fraud-risk indicators or the Do Not Pay system.
claims.sourceSpan: based on an output of the Do Not Pay system under section 3354
claims.note: Fraud-risk indicator: 3337(a)(1); Do Not Pay: 3337(b) and def. 3337(j)(2).

claims.claim: Payee Protections
claims.sourceSpan: Payee Notification and Time Limit of Paused Disbursement

claims.claim: Payee notified and given a chance to contest.
claims.sourceSpan: to contest any factual inaccuracy or provide clarifying information during the corrective action review period

claims.claim: Payment due within 30 days of the determination.
claims.sourceSpan: Issue such payment not later than 30 days after a determination to take a corrective action is made by the head of the agency

claims.claim: Routine, low-risk portions allowed to proceed.
claims.sourceSpan: the head of each agency shall allow a routine, historically consistent payment amount to proceed while temporarily holding an anomalous, unusually large, or high-risk portion of a payment

claims.claim: Names the Act the "Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act".
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the
claims.note: Title text: "Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act".

claims.claim: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act

claims.claim: Authorizes agencies and the Treasury to pause, condition, or segment federal payments that present an elevated fraud risk.
claims.sourceSpan: temporarily delay, condition, or segment a disbursement request

claims.claim: Adds Section 3337 to title 31.
claims.sourceSpan: Subchapter II of chapter 33 of title 31, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following
claims.note: New "Sec. 3337" inserted.

claims.claim: Before certifying a payment voucher, an agency must temporarily delay, condition, or segment a disbursement that an official determines presents an elevated risk of fraud or improper payment.
claims.sourceSpan: The head of an agency shall take a corrective action to temporarily delay, condition, or segment a disbursement request before the certification of a payment voucher under section 3325

claims.claim: or when ordered by the Treasury.
claims.sourceSpan: has been notified of an order from the Secretary of the Treasury described under subsection (b)

claims.claim: The Treasury may return a certified voucher and issue a corrective-action order based on a fraud-risk indicator or a Do Not Pay system flag.
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary shall promptly notify the relevant certifying official of an order to return a certified payment voucher submitted to a disbursing official under section 3325 and issue a corrective action order to the head of an agency
claims.note: Do Not Pay basis: "based on an output of the Do Not Pay system under section 3354".

claims.claim: Actions must be objective, narrowly applied, and time-limited.
claims.sourceSpan: be narrowly applied to the portion of the payment presenting the elevated risk
claims.note: Objective: "be based on an objective, documented fraud-risk indicator"; time-limited: "be limited in duration to the minimum period necessary".

claims.claim: the payee must be notified and given a process to contest.
claims.sourceSpan: to contest any factual inaccuracy or provide clarifying information during the corrective action review period

claims.claim: the payment must be issued within 30 days of the determination (or 7 days after the payee contests).
claims.sourceSpan: but not later than 7 days after the date on which the payee contests the corrective action
claims.note: 30-day: "Issue such payment not later than 30 days after a determination..."; 7-day span quoted here.

claims.claim: Routine, historically consistent payment amounts may proceed while an anomalous portion is held.
claims.sourceSpan: the head of each agency shall allow a routine, historically consistent payment amount to proceed while temporarily holding an anomalous, unusually large, or high-risk portion of a payment

claims.claim: Law-enforcement exemptions and good-faith liability protection apply.
claims.sourceSpan: No officer or employee of the Federal Government shall be personally liable for an action taken in good faith under this section
claims.note: Law-enforcement exemption: "Exemptions for Law Enforcement Activities" 3337(f).

claims.claim: the Treasury must issue implementing regulations within 180 days.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this section, and annually thereafter, the Secretary, in consultation with the Director, shall issue regulations
claims.note: Secretary = Treasury.

claims.claim: The Treasury must also report to Congress 18 months after enactment, and annually thereafter.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter, the Secretary of the Treasury shall submit
claims.note: Report recipients: OMB Director + 4 congressional committees; "to Congress" is an acceptable gloss.

claims.claim: reporting on the number of orders issued, the share of paused payments ultimately paid, and total savings.
claims.sourceSpan: The total number of orders to return a certified payment voucher
claims.note: Share paid: "The percentage of such payments that are issued by the agency"; savings: "The total savings to the Federal Government in payments determined to be fraudulent".

claims.claim: the amendments take effect 1 year after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: The amendments made by this section shall take effect 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Introduced by Rep. Comer (R-KY).
claims.note: Sponsor/party is cache metadata (matches sponsor field "Rep. Comer, James (R-KY)"); the bill source names no sponsor. Structural metadata carve-out per rubric class 8; not verifiable from bill text.

claims.claim: the bill has not yet received a Senate vote.
claims.sourceSpan: Passed the House of Representatives June 10, 2026
claims.note: Structural: source shows only House passage; votes[] has no Senate vote; stage=house.

claims.claim: Authority for agencies and the Treasury to pause, condition, or segment fraud-risk federal payments, with payee notice and a 30-day limit (new Section 3337 of title 31).
claims.sourceSpan: Subchapter II of chapter 33 of title 31, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following

claims.claim: Relief of accountable officers (Section 3527 of title 31) extended to good-faith actions under the new pause authority.
claims.sourceSpan: was made as a result of a good faith effort to comply with the requirements of section 3337
claims.note: Section 3527 amended: "Section 3527 of title 31, United States Code, is amended".

claims.claim: The bill sets a 30-day limit to issue a paused payment but does not specify a consequence if an agency misses it.
claims.sourceSpan: Issue such payment not later than 30 days after a determination to take a corrective action is made by the head of the agency
claims.note: 30-day limit present; no penalty/consequence for missing it appears anywhere in the text (verifiable absence).

claims.claim: It relies on fraud-risk indicators and the Do Not Pay system but does not address erroneous flags that wrongly delay legitimate payments beyond the contest process.
claims.sourceSpan: match identified by the Do Not Pay system under section 3354
claims.note: Contest process = 3337(d)(2). Interpretive but grounded: 2(f)(2) requires "recommendations to mitigate such errors in the fraud-risk indicators" prospectively, not a payee remedy for a wrongful flag.

claims.claim: Conforming amendments to disbursing officials (section 3325(a)(3)) and certifying officials (section 3528) not surfaced in changes.
claims.sourceSpan: section 3528 of title 31, United States Code, is amended
claims.note: Bill also amends 3325(a)(3) and 3528 (incl. relief of certifying officials for good-faith 3337 compliance); changes lists only 3527. Parallel/technical; captured in versionChanges. Not material.

claims.claim: State/local-government-official notification trigger (3337(a)(2)) for State-administered, federally-funded programs not surfaced in prose.
claims.sourceSpan: notification by the relevant State or local government official
claims.note: A distinct trigger; still the agency acting on a State/local notification. Captured in versionChanges. Minor.

claims.claim: Rule of construction (3337(h)) and the "not a final determination of eligibility/liability/wrongdoing" clause (3337(g)) not surfaced.
claims.sourceSpan: not constitute a final determination of eligibility, liability, or wrongdoing
claims.note: Rule of construction: "Nothing in this section may be construed to supersede any other provision of law". Technical/protective nuance; minor.

notes: Source = Engrossed in House (EH) text, full read. No referencedSources registered. No material errors: every figure (2/7/30-day, 180-day, 18-month, 1-year), actor (agency head vs Treasury Secretary), and direction (mandatory pause; segmentation permits low-risk to proceed) checks out. Minor items: soft plain-English gloss on the conditional 30-day issuance in summary; unsourced breadth-of-support framing + sponsor/cosponsor metadata in likelihoodReason (structural carve-out); three minor coverage omissions (3325(a)(3)/3528 conforming amendments, State/local trigger, rule-of-construction/non-final-determination clauses).
